data.title: Chlorhexidine (0.5–4%)
data.category: More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics_

**Class:** Bisbiguanide antiseptic

## Mechanism of action
- Cationic molecule binds and disrupts bacterial membranes; residual (persistent) activity on skin for hours

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Pre-operative skin preparation (with alcohol — preferred), hand hygiene, body washes for MRSA decolonisation and recurrent furunculosis, mouthwash (0.12–0.2%), umbilical cord care (7.1% gel)

## Dose & formulations
- Body wash 4% daily for 5 days (with nasal mupirocin) for recurrent boils

## Adverse effects
- Irritation, contact dermatitis, contact urticaria and anaphylaxis (an increasingly recognised allergen)
- Ototoxicity if it enters the middle ear; keratitis (eyes); tooth staining (mouthwash)

## Contraindications
- Eyes, ears (perforated drum), meninges

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Persistent activity — preferred pre-op antisepsis with alcohol
- Can cause anaphylaxis (chlorhexidine-coated catheters)

_Sources: Khopkar ch.30 (Chlorhexidine). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
